title: Yehudah Ish Chotzi
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Yerushalmi Sheviit, chapter 5, halakhah 5, relates that he secluded himself in a cave for three days to consider why the lives of the people of his own city take precedence over those of another city. Rabbi Yosi ben Chalafta came to him. Rabbi Yosi summoned his son R' Avirdomas, and he explained the reason to him. In [Nedarim, chapter 11, at the end of halakhah 1](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Nedarim.11.1.7), a scribal error has crept in. In any case, I have already explained in the entry Isi ben Yehudah how the Yerushalmi should read.[^1]

notes.text: שנטמן means that the subject secluded himself, not that an unnamed person was buried. וקרא means summoned, not named, and בריה explicitly marks the son. The final “he explained to him” preserves the pronouns without supplying new recipients. Hyman identifies a scribal error here without supplying its corrected name in this notice; the following abbreviation is discussed in note 3. The final first-person cross-reference remains Hyman’s own. סה״א is read contextually as the end of halakhah 1. Avirdomas follows the supplied proofread אבירדומס; the older OCR spelling is not substituted.

Guggenheimer’s Jerusalem Talmud, Nedarim 11:1:7, has the same cave discussion and explicitly names Rabbi Yosi ben Chalafta. It calls the summoned son Rabbi Abba, not Hyman’s Avirdomas, and its arrival wording also differs from the supplied Hyman notice. Hyman’s name and account remain in the body, with R' for Avirdomas: Rabbi Abba’s title is not transferred to a different name. Hyman’s Sheviit 5:5 locator could not be retrieved in this bounded check; its earlier unconfirmed link is removed while the printed locator remains. No replacement Sheviit location or corrected name is asserted.

The accepted Hebrew transcription has מ״ם after ט״ס, which the earlier English interpreted as “the letter mem.” The native page boundary instead reads ט״ס at the foot of printed page 552, followed by מ״מ, וכבר בארתי at the top of page 553. Here מ״מ is read as מכל מקום, “in any case,” introducing Hyman’s cross-reference to his Isi ben Yehudah entry. The English corrects that earlier interpretation; it does not change the accepted Hebrew transcription or identify the particular textual error. This is a bounded reading of the page-boundary phrase, not a fresh proofread of the whole notice.
